item.description: NPR critics remember some of their favorite Dolly performances — including a duet with Kermit the Frog and the twinkle in Dolly's eye singing with Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris.

item.title: Before an emergency hearing, the Kennedy Center's board threatens to demolish it
item.description: A lawsuit seeks to block President Trump's name from going back on the center. The center's board warns that if renovation plans don't go forward, it may be demolished.

item.title: Yayoi Kusama, high priestess of polka dots, has died
item.description: The Japanese artist has died at age 97. Kusama's polka dotted pumpkins, "Infinity Rooms," and other repetitive and dreamlike artworks have been shown in museums and galleries worldwide.

item.title: Tim Curry, who defined 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show,' has died
item.description: Curry will be most remembered for his role as Dr. Frank-N-Furter, the tyrannical gender-bending alien scientist in both stage and screen versions of The Rocky Horror Picture Show. He was 80.

item.title: Dolly Parton lived her motto: 'More is more'
item.description: "I've always believed that a part of my magic, if there was any, was the fact that I look so artificial — but I am so totally real," Parton said in 2001.

item.title: How Dolly Parton wrote the story of a changing America
item.description: Parton, who died at 80 on Tuesday, had charm, depth, beauty, wit and radiant goodness. She was also a songwriter whose work told the story not just of country music but of the country itself.

item.title: 'Life of M' constructs a portrait of how stardom hides a person's core
item.description: Like much of Rachel Cusk's work, Life of M is driven by her concern with conditions that impede self-definition -- for writers, artists, and women in particular.

item.title: Hollywood's summer box office is glowing, but the numbers come with startling caveats
item.description: Theaters have had something for everyone this summer, and fans are paying top dollar for premium formats like IMAX. There are also fewer moviegoers, fewer movies and fewer screens than there were pre-COVID.
